body:
`createSessionTable` in `src/server/session.ts` (SPEC §36.4, landed by T125/PR #289) is a second, unused implementation of session and token bookkeeping. Nothing imports it except `test/server/session-table.test.ts`, which is a FROZEN RAIL of the archived ticket T125. The shipped login doors (§36.5/§36.6) and the bearer bridge (§36.7) run their own `Map<string, BrowserSession>` inside `makeUserDoors`, and the token half lives in `src/server/http.ts`.

THE DEFECT IS THE GREEN BAR, NOT THE DEAD CODE. `test/server/session-table.test.ts` passes, proving monotonic-clock, idle-sweep, cap-refuses-not-evicts and digest-revocation semantics for code that no request executes. A reader of a green run reads it as evidence about the shipped door. It is not. That is the H7 shape at the rail layer: a report that is true about the artifact it names and false about the thing the reader cares about.

THE DECISION: DELETE, not route. Two options existed.

(a) Route the doors' bookkeeping through `createSessionTable`, making its rails live. REJECTED. The two halves have diverged for reasons the shipped design holds deliberately, and the table has no slot for any of them:
  - A door session carries `roles` and a `formToken`. `SessionRow` carries neither.
  - `resolveToken` answers a USERNAME string. The shipped bridge answers a `TokenIdentity` (`{ operator: true }`) — server-wide authority, not a named user.
  - The shipped bridge re-asks `otherWorlds()` and a `stillLive()` callback on EVERY presentation, so a container that mounts itself closes an already-minted token. The table has no such hook and could not grow one without becoming the doors' code with extra steps.
  - The token table lives in `http.ts` because that is where the bearer header is read. Moving it into a session object would put the resolver a layer away from its only caller.
Routing would mean rewriting the table into the doors' shape, on a shipped authentication path, to salvage a rail that already has a live equivalent. That trades real risk for no coverage.

(b) Delete `createSessionTable` and retire its rail. TAKEN.

THE COVERAGE MAP that justifies retiring the rail. Every property the frozen rail proves is already proved of the SHIPPED path, against real HTTP traffic:

| T125 criterion | live rail |
|---|---|
| 1. refuses a session past its idle window | `login-door.test.ts` (o) |
| 2. a clock backstep cannot revive it | `login-door.test.ts` (o) |
| 3. a restart invalidates every session | structural — see the gap below |
| 4. holds at most its cap, never evicts a live session, reclaims an abandoned one | `login-door.test.ts` (p) |
| 5. a token is a DIGEST with its own TTL, isolated from the session window | `session-token.test.ts` (e), (f2) |
| 6. dropping a session revokes the tokens it minted | `session-token.test.ts` (f) — all four drop paths |
| (audit) per-session live-token cap refuses and recovers | `session-token.test.ts` (g) |
| (audit) an already-minted token stops being honored | `session-token.test.ts` (i2) |

THE ONE GAP, NAMED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. Criterion 3 (a restart invalidates every session) has no live rail. It had none worth having in the frozen rail either: that test constructed two tables and observed that the second did not know the first's ids, which is a restatement of `new Map()` rather than a property of the code. The shipped doors hold the same structural guarantee for the same reason — `sessions` is a closure-local `Map` inside `makeUserDoors`, allocated per `serve()` call, with no persistence path. This ticket does not add a rail for it, and §36.4's corrected text says so plainly.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. Each names its verification.

1. `createSessionTable` and its private types are gone from `src/server/session.ts`. Verified by `grep -rn 'createSessionTable\|SessionTableOptions\|SessionRow\|TokenEntry' src test` returning nothing.
2. `test/server/session-table.test.ts` no longer exists. Verified by `test -e test/server/session-table.test.ts` exiting non-zero.
3. The whole suite is green with the file gone — no live rail depended on the deleted export. Verified by `npm run check`, reading the counts.
4. T125's `rails` array is empty in `.adlc/ticket-archive/`, written through `adlc ticket update --authorize` rather than by hand. Verified by `adlc ticket show T125 --json | jq '.ticket.rails'` printing `[]`, and by the recorded transaction.
5. SPEC §36.4 describes what SHIPPED: the session map inside the login doors, the token table in `http.ts`, and the fact that phase 4's standalone table was retired. Its Provenance footer names this PR alongside #289 and points at the live rails. Verified by reading `spec/36-users-and-sessions.md` §36.4 and by `test/site/capabilities.test.ts`.
6. No `{says, spec, proof}` claim in `demos/capabilities/chapters.mjs` cites the deleted rail. Verified by `grep -n 'session-table' demos/capabilities/chapters.mjs` returning nothing, and by `test/site/capabilities.test.ts` green.
7. No comment anywhere still promises the phase-4 table as a live thing a later phase will meet. Verified by `grep -rn 'phase-4 .SessionTable.\|createSessionTable' src test .adlc/specs` returning only historical mentions in §36.4's own working spec, which is an archived design artifact and stays as written.

WHO MERGES IT. This is a REPAIR: it removes an untrue claim and deletes code no request runs. It changes nothing the system promises on the wire, widens no door, and purges no data. Self-merge on the ordinary bar — `npm run check` green, P5 clean, post-work audit clean — with the rail retirement stated in the PR body per CLAUDE.md.

PROVENANCE OF THE FINDING. An independent premortem during T128 (§36 phase 7) found it, and `.adlc/specs/36-07-the-bearer-bridge.md` named it as a known gap rather than fixing it there, because retiring another ticket's frozen rail was not that phase's to do.
title: Retire `createSessionTable` — a dead implementation with living tests
